newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks shrug off weak GDP to end firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks shrug off weak GDP to end firm.

text.p: The Singapore stock market shrugged off an overnight announcement of weaker economic data to end firmer on Wednesday, dealers said.
"I was quite surprised the market ended higher after the figures. Obviously, the view is for the market to move higher," a dealer at a foreign institution said.
Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said on Tuesday evening that Singapore's third quarter growth was just 3.2 percent against 7.5 percent in second quarter.
He revised down the country's 1996 growth forecast to around six percent from seven to eight percent previously.

But after trading down to a low of 2,064.12, the Straits Times Industrials Index rebounded to end at 2,080.45, up 10.22 points. Turnover was at 89.5 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 163 to 127.
Singapore Press Holdings led gainers after rising S$0.70 on a technical rebound to end at S$24.20.
"The consensus is that the worse is over and investors were looking to buy, including a U.S. house," said the dealer. But he cautioned against too much optimism since the buying was light.
Sembawang Corp rose S$0.35 to end at S$6.45 on renewed optimism over the stock. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
